## 1.0.5 (2026-11-11)

1.0.4 was tagged but its build never published, so this release carries its changes. A security and reliability release: two-factor codes can no longer be guessed over time, a tenant can no longer stall or crash the worker, and the dashboard keeps up with what the server holds. Three database migrations run on update.

### Security
- Two-factor codes share one limit per account across sign in, step-up and turning two-factor off. Ten wrong codes lock the account for 15 minutes, each lockout in a row doubles (up to 24 hours), the count survives restarts and updates, and the account's owner gets an email on the first lockout.
- Previews are kept per repository and pull request. Two repositories in one project no longer share a preview, so closing a pull request in one can never tear down the other's. Whether a preview builds a fork's commit is fixed when the build is queued.
- Build output in a failed deploy notice can no longer carry a live link to chat or email.
- Viewers and read tokens no longer see Vercel build and install commands, backup destinations, bucket names, provider errors or the backup key fingerprint. Project-limited tokens no longer see the owner's email.
- Dockify's own update dump can no longer be downloaded, restored or swept as an orphaned backup.
- Status page feeds ignore a forwarded host sent by the client.
- The container firewall rules now load before Docker starts after a reboot. Uninstall removes the new unit.
- A rollback to the previous release is trusted only within the rollback window.
- Images whose labels exceed 64 KB are refused before a container is created.

### Fixed
- A tenant database could crash the worker through the data browser, or stall every project's backups by holding a lock. Data jobs now have deadlines, pg_dump waits at most 5 minutes for a lock, dumps respect backpressure, and the data browser and SQL console read within fixed bounds. The SQL console runs one statement per request.
- Restore downloads stop at the backup's recorded size. Restore errors no longer include table rows.
- Sites that declare only an SVG icon now get their favicon: it is sanitized and served like an SVG logo. Emails and pull request comments show the default icon for those.
- A favicon that is missing now says so ("/favicon.ico answered 404") instead of reporting a size or format error.
- Notifications are ordered by time, "Mark as read" sticks with several tabs open, and the update notice no longer shows for the version already running.
- The Variables tables keep every key on one line, with the lock beside it.
- After adding or removing an environment, the Variables tab shows that environment's variables.
- Saving a build branch or image no longer jumps back to the old value.
- The sidebar, the command menu and the tab title follow the server on every page. Project pages, the Deployments filter, Domains, Resources, Activity and the Settings lists refresh after a change.
- Saving the Notifications settings no longer pins the preview domain as custom. Each settings section saves only its own fields.
- The Backups page reads the last 30 days by date, and a bulk backup that starts nothing says so.
- Alert history says 90 days, as it shows. A webhook test that never reached the endpoint no longer marks the webhook failing.

### Changed
- The theme toggle no longer plays a sound.

## 1.0.3 (2026-11-08)

Project icons start as the folder, the version is right after an in-app update, and the local backup warning says what to do.

### Changed
- A project's icon is now the folder unless you choose otherwise. The Icon dropdown offers Folder (the default), each frontend with a fetched favicon, and the uploaded image while there is one. Automatic is gone: a project on Automatic shows the folder after the update, and a project set to an app's favicon or to an upload keeps it. If the chosen app is deleted or loses its favicon, the project shows the folder. Apps still fetch their favicons as before.

### Fixed
- After an in-app update, the version some places read stayed at the version first installed, because the updater rewrites only `release/release.env` and `.env` kept the old `DOCKIFY_VERSION`. Dockify now reads the version baked into the image it runs, so the agent, the update checks, the update notices and Settings all name the running version. The Settings menu now shows the version too; it showed none before.
- The "On this server" backup tier said to add S3 compatible storage even when storage was set up and the Offsite tier was on. The warning now shows only while a database's copies stay on this server, and says to turn on the Offsite tier when storage exists, or to add storage first when it does not.

## 1.0.2 (2026-11-08)

Projects as folders of apps, two backup tiers, project icons you can pick, and apps that reach each other by name.

### Added
- Every app answers to its name on its environment's network, so a frontend can call `http://backend:3020`. Before, only managed services had their name; built and image apps answered only to their `dk-<id>` address. The display name never becomes an address. An app takes its name on its next deploy.
- Two backup tiers per database: On this server (this server's disk) and Offsite (an S3 destination). Each has its own schedule, its own switch and its own number of backups to keep. When both are due together they share one dump, and each copy succeeds or fails on its own. Back up now writes to every tier that is on. The Backups tab and the Backups page show and edit both tiers.
- A project's Icon section is a dropdown: Automatic, which names the app it picks, each frontend with a fetched favicon, and the uploaded image while there is one.

### Changed
- A project is a folder of apps, and environments are optional. A new project starts with production only, and a project with one environment shows no environment tags, switchers or pickers anywhere. With two or more, the project header has an environment switcher. Settings adds and removes environments, and never removes the last one.
- Backups are kept by count: the newest N good automatic backups per tier. A failed run never counts, and the only good copy is never removed. Upgrading moves each database's schedule to the tier its destination names, with its cron, its switch and its old rule ("keep 3 and N days"). Clear the days in the schedule dialog to keep by count alone.
- On Automatic, a project's icon is the favicon of its most public frontend: the production frontend on a custom domain first, so an admin panel on a test domain no longer wins over the public site.
- Icon images fill their box with no background behind them, so transparent logos stay transparent.

### Fixed
- Each release made a Vercel project that builds the site from this repository try to deploy the releases branch and fail. That branch now tells Vercel not to deploy it.
- A deployment deleted on Vercel stayed in Dockify's list of an app that follows Vercel. Dockify now asks Vercel about it and removes it once Vercel confirms it is gone.

## 1.0.1 (2026-11-07)

Rename apps, a fuller view of apps that follow Vercel, and fixes for Vercel logs and Cloudflare tokens.

### Added
- Rename an app. Settings has a Name section for the name the dashboard, notifications, emails and pull request comments show. The app's original name stays its identity for containers, volumes, links, preview hosts and the CLI, so nothing is redeployed. Two apps in one environment cannot show the same name.
- An app that follows Vercel now reads its Vercel project live. Overview shows what production serves (domains, commit, branch, author, build time) and the project settings, Variables lists the project's environment variables (an admin sees plain values, encrypted and sensitive values are never shown), and Domains lists the project's domains on Vercel. Each tab links to manage it on Vercel.

### Changed
- Counts in group headings are in brackets, so a count after a date, as in "Sat 7 Nov (19)", no longer reads as part of it.

### Fixed
- The Logs tab of an app that follows Vercel could keep showing "Too many log reads" after you switched tabs, because a read for a page you had left kept its slot. A read now stops the moment you leave, and the tab says plainly when Vercel has no runtime logs.
- Connecting a Cloudflare token with only zone permissions failed with "This token cannot see any Cloudflare account". Dockify now takes the account from the token's zones.
- After `install.sh --upgrade` from the signed feed, Settings, Updates could still ask to set DOCKIFY_RELEASE_FEED on an install made without a feed. The upgrade now records the feed and key that checked the new images in `.env`.

## 1.0.0 (2026-11-07)

The first release: one server, safe deploys, tested backups and a locked-down control plane.

### Added
- Install on one fresh Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 server with one command. The installer checks the signed release and pulls images by digest.
- Push to deploy from GitHub, per branch, with live build logs and a step timeline.
- Zero-downtime deploys for stateless apps, gated on a health check, with automatic rollback.
- Rollback by image id, with no rebuild.
- Release commands for migrations, run before traffic moves.
- Managed Postgres and Redis, plus S3 storage, private by default.
- Six templates: Gotify, ntfy, Memos, SeaweedFS, Uptime Kuma and Miniflux.
- Preview deploys per pull request, removed when it closes. Forks build only if you opt in, and never get secrets.
- Encrypted backups to local disk or your S3-compatible bucket, with scheduled restore tests.
- Restore from the dashboard, into a new database by default.
- Alert rules per app for down, crash loops and memory, plus host disk, sent to Discord, Slack, Teams, a signed webhook and more, or by email.
- Email over your own SMTP server for invites, password resets, security notices, alerts and failed deploys.
- Disk cleanup that keeps rollback images, and a disk alert at 85% by default.
- Domains through a Cloudflare tunnel with DNS done for you, or direct mode with Let's Encrypt.
- Env vars per environment, with history and rollback.
- Streaming logs, and CPU, memory and disk graphs per app.
- Import of projects and env vars from Vercel.
- Teams with Admin and Viewer roles.
- API tokens with expiry, scopes and a project limit.
- Signed self-updates that dump the database first and roll back on their own.

### Security
- 2FA, a session list and an audit log. Changing what runs asks for your 2FA code again.
- Builds and deploys reach Docker only through a gate that allows the calls they need and refuses the rest, including pulls from internal and cloud metadata addresses.
- One container builder: capabilities dropped, never privileged, no host network, folders or ports.
- Each secret sealed on its own with AES-256-GCM. The master key never enters the database.
- Every API route has a declared policy, and a test fails if one is missing.
- The installer refuses a runtime with known escape bugs and blocks containers from cloud metadata addresses.
